project.title: Integrated Security and Access Control Upgrade for Multi-Site Facility
project.objective: Plan and roll out a standardized security and access control procedure across all facility zones to reduce incidents and improve response time.
deliverables: Standard operating procedures for access control and patrols
Shift handover and incident logging checklist
Training session plan and attendance records
constraints: All changes must comply with legal requirements related to ammunition and use-of-force
Procedures must align with fire safety and evacuation regulations
Minimal disruption to visitors, staff, and deliveries during rollout
New routines must be feasible with current headcount and shifts
Documentation must protect sensitive and security-classified information

risks.risk: Guards resist adopting new patrol and access routines.
risks.mitigation: Involve guards in drafting procedures, run short practical trainings, and collect feedback for quick adjustments.

risks.risk: New procedures conflict with existing fire safety or evacuation plans.
risks.mitigation: Review all drafts with Health and Safety Officer and fire safety guidelines before approval.

risks.risk: Inconsistent incident logging leads to unreliable data.
risks.mitigation: Introduce a simple checklist-based log, train all shifts, and spot-check logs in the first weeks.

risks.risk: Visitors and staff experience delays at entry points.
risks.mitigation: Pilot new access checks in one zone, measure queue times, and adjust staffing or steps before full rollout.

risks.risk: Sensitive security information is shared over unsecured channels.
risks.mitigation: Define clear rules on what can be shared in chat, and store detailed plans only in controlled-access documents.

themes.why_relevant: Better routes reduce blind spots and response time while keeping workload realistic for each shift.
Standardized checks at gates and doors reduce unauthorized access and confusion for visitors.
Clear logging and escalation rules improve coordination with authorities and management.
Former post experience helps design safe, efficient handling of packages and cargo inspections.
Consistent procedures for fire, medical, and security incidents reduce risk and liability.

backlog.task: Conduct baseline security risk walk-through for all facility zones
definition_of_done: All main zones (commercial, industrial, parking, hospital-like areas, ships/ports if applicable) inspected
Key risks and blind spots listed with photos or sketches
Findings consolidated into the risk assessment report draft

backlog.task: Draft standard operating procedures for access control at main entrances
definition_of_done: Entry check steps defined for staff, visitors, and deliveries
Procedures cover ID checks, bag checks, and illegal substances handling
Draft reviewed for compliance with legal requirements and information security policies

backlog.task: Design standard patrol routes and schedules for day and night shifts
definition_of_done: Patrol routes mapped for each zone with estimated timings
Routes include checks for fire safety equipment and access points
Routes validated as feasible with current staffing and shift patterns

backlog.task: Create incident logging and shift handover checklist
definition_of_done: Checklist covers incident type, time, location, actions taken, and escalation
Handover section includes open issues and watch points
Checklist tested by at least one full shift and refined based on feedback

backlog.task: Define escalation matrix for security, medical, and fire incidents
definition_of_done: Clear levels of severity defined for each incident type
Contact chain documented for internal and external authorities
Matrix aligned with legal use-of-force and first aid protocols

backlog.task: Standardize procedures for inspecting cargo, packages, and mail
definition_of_done: Inspection steps documented for different package types
Guidance on suspicious items and illegal substances included
Process coordinated with mail and delivery staff to avoid delays

backlog.task: Prepare emergency response and evacuation playbook
definition_of_done: Scenarios covered: fire, active threat, medical emergency, hazardous materials
Roles and responsibilities for guards and staff defined
Playbook reviewed with Health and Safety Officer

backlog.task: Plan and schedule short training sessions for all guards
definition_of_done: Training agenda created covering new SOPs and checklists
Sessions scheduled to cover all shifts without gaps in coverage
Attendance recorded and open questions captured

backlog.task: Pilot new access and patrol procedures in one high-risk zone
definition_of_done: Pilot zone selected and communicated
New procedures followed for at least one full week
Issues and incident data collected and summarized

backlog.task: Summarize incident trends before and after rollout
definition_of_done: Baseline incident data collected for previous period
Post-rollout data collected for comparable period
Simple comparison report created with key observations

artifacts.title: Standard Operating Procedures for Access Control and Patrols
artifacts.used_for: Reference for guards on how to perform entry checks, patrols, and radio communication.

artifacts.title: Incident Logging and Shift Handover Checklist
artifacts.used_for: Ensures consistent recording of incidents and smooth handover between shifts.

artifacts.title: Emergency Response and Escalation Playbook
artifacts.used_for: Defines steps and contacts for fire, medical, and security emergencies.

artifacts.title: Training Schedule and Attendance Tracker
artifacts.used_for: Plans training sessions across shifts and records who has been trained.

artifacts.title: Cargo, Package, and Mail Inspection Checklist
artifacts.used_for: Guides guards through safe and compliant inspection of deliveries and mail.

artifacts.title: Incident Trend Comparison Summary
artifacts.used_for: Stores before-and-after incident counts to evaluate impact of new procedures.

threads_plan.thread_goal: Align on current issues and finalize scope for the security upgrade project.
threads_plan.trigger: Kickoff message announcing the project and asking guards to share main pain points and risks.

mandatory_decisions.decision: Agree on the list of priority zones to include in the first phase of the upgrade.
Confirm what types of incidents must always be logged using the new checklist.

threads_plan.thread_goal: Design and agree on new access control and patrol procedures.
threads_plan.trigger: Post initial draft of access control and patrol SOPs for review and comments.

mandatory_decisions.decision: Approve the standard steps for staff, visitor, and delivery access checks.
Lock in the final patrol routes and frequency for day and night shifts.

threads_plan.thread_goal: Finalize incident logging, shift handover, and escalation rules.
threads_plan.trigger: Share draft incident logging checklist and escalation matrix for feedback.

mandatory_decisions.decision: Approve the incident logging and shift handover checklist format.
Agree on the escalation levels and who to contact for each severity.

threads_plan.thread_goal: Plan the pilot rollout and training sessions for guards.
threads_plan.trigger: Message proposing pilot zone, training dates, and asking for shift constraints.

mandatory_decisions.decision: Select the zone where the new procedures will be piloted first.
Confirm the final training schedule covering all shifts.

threads_plan.thread_goal: Review pilot results and agree on adjustments before full rollout.
threads_plan.trigger: Post summary of pilot incidents and feedback after the first week.

channel_rituals: Daily async start-of-shift check-in summarizing key watch points and known issues.
End-of-shift summary post highlighting incidents logged and any handover notes.
Weekly review message to discuss incident trends and propose small procedure tweaks.
Post-incident debrief thread for any major event to capture lessons learned.
Pre-weekend coordination post to align on high-traffic events and staffing focus.
